plan_a_advantages: Includes a dedicated tempo run for threshold development.
Long runs are strategically spaced and focused on endurance and trail durability.
More frequent easy runs promote recovery and adaptation.
plan_b_advantages: Hill session provides targeted strength work.
Longer total duration across the week (though this is partially offset by more easy runs).
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates a dedicated tempo run, which is crucial for developing sustainable threshold strength – a key determinant of running speed. Plan B, while including a hill session, lacks this specific type of workout. Furthermore, Plan A’s long runs are strategically placed to build endurance and trail durability, while Plan B’s long runs are more consistently easy, potentially limiting the stimulus for improvement. Finally, the shorter, more frequent easy runs in Plan A allow for better recovery and adaptation between harder sessions.
